title: Next 50 Most Needed AXM Modules

basis.qualityDirection: PS2 floor, then evidence-gated PS3 and PS4 rungs
basis.rankingRule: Remove current-module duplicates, then rank by playable-value unlocked, reuse across games, bottleneck severity, local-first feasibility, and proofability.

constraints: No mandatory cloud, CDN, paid service, proprietary runtime, or third-party package.
Build AXM-native primitives first; optional free/open-source adapters remain isolated and replaceable.
Every module emits versioned machine-readable contracts, deterministic recipes where applicable, exact provenance, and bounded failure receipts.
A preview, label, file count, or green syntax test never proves visual, audio, gameplay, performance, accessibility, or release quality.
Human approval remains required for promoted assets, public releases, rights decisions, destructive changes, and expanded authority.
New modules extend existing parents and services; they do not create duplicate replacement Hubs.

phases.name: Playable 3D foundation
phases.exit: One Forge asset family runs in a local 3D game loop with matching materials, animation, measurable budgets, and exact import receipts.

phases.name: PS3-capable content factory
phases.exit: A coherent street, character, vehicle, terrain, effects, and lighting set passes independent technical checks and Mike's visual gate.

phases.name: Complete game loop
phases.exit: A small game supports UI, quests, save/replay, multiplayer, accessibility, automated playtesting, and human-reviewed balance evidence.

phases.name: Independent production substrate
phases.exit: Builds, codecs, migrations, jobs, crashes, merges, and fuzz checks run locally with no required third-party runtime.

phases.name: Public release discipline
phases.exit: A rights-cleared, reproducible, compact, documented, localized package passes sandbox certification before explicit release.

modules.name: Local 3D Game Runtime
modules.purpose: Turn Forge and Spatial Studio GLB scenes into an actual playable offline 3D loop with cameras, animation, scene lifecycle, world snapshots, controls, and deterministic ticks.
modules.whyNow: Assets cannot become games until one authoritative runtime can play them; the existing Game Forge is strongest in 2D and packaging.
modules.firstBuild: Load one approved Forge street and animated pedestrian, walk through it with keyboard and controller, and bind read-only Living World state.
acceptance: No runtime network request
Imported GLB materials and animations match the Forge reference
Deterministic tick and frame-time receipt exist
Runtime cannot reset authoritative world state

modules.name: Asset ↔ Engine Round-trip Bridge
modules.purpose: Validate and translate units, axes, pivots, materials, textures, skins, animations, LODs, collision, metadata, and source digests between authoring and runtime contracts.
modules.whyNow: A beautiful asset is still unusable when engine import silently changes scale, shading, animation, or collision.
modules.firstBuild: Round-trip the storefront and animated pedestrian through the 3D runtime without editing source files.
acceptance: Before/after structural diff is machine-readable
Scale, orientation, material, rig, and animation parity pass
Losses are explicit instead of hidden
Original source digest remains attached

modules.name: PBR Material Baker
modules.purpose: Author and bake albedo, normal, roughness, metalness, ambient-occlusion, emissive, height, and packed channel maps from editable material recipes.
modules.whyNow: This is the largest direct jump from PS2-style surfaces toward credible PS3 assets.
modules.firstBuild: Bake brick, asphalt, painted metal, glass, skin, and vehicle paint families using local CPU/WebGL paths.
acceptance: Maps contain real non-flat signal
Tangent-space convention is declared and verified
Packed channels decode independently
Reference renders pass human material review

modules.name: Mesh Retopology & Optimizer
modules.purpose: Create game-ready topology, repair normals and manifolds, weld seams, simplify meshes, and preserve silhouettes and deformation-critical loops.
modules.whyNow: Source meshes need controllable topology and budgets before higher-detail assets can run in games.
modules.firstBuild: Optimize one building, vehicle, and rigged pedestrian with protected boundaries and named budget targets.
acceptance: Triangle reduction is measured
Silhouette error stays below the declared bound
UVs and material groups survive
Rig deformation is visually compared before promotion

modules.name: UV & Lightmap Studio
modules.purpose: Create and inspect texture UVs and second-channel lightmap UVs with islands, seams, padding, overlap, distortion, and texel-density controls.
modules.whyNow: Texture and lighting quality cannot scale without predictable UV space.
modules.firstBuild: Produce validated primary and lightmap UV sets for the storefront family.
acceptance: Overlap and out-of-range islands are reported
Texel density is measurable
Padding survives target mip levels
Checker and baked-light previews are visually verified

modules.name: LOD, HLOD & Impostor Builder
modules.purpose: Generate bounded LOD chains, grouped HLODs, billboard and octahedral impostors, transition metadata, and reversible source receipts.
modules.whyNow: Large GTA- or Diablo-like worlds require distance-scaled asset cost rather than rendering every source at full detail.
modules.firstBuild: Create three LODs and one impostor for a building, vehicle, tree, and pedestrian.
acceptance: Every level meets its triangle target
Screen-space transition error is measured
Material and pivot continuity pass
Pop and silhouette changes receive live visual review

modules.name: Technical Art Validator
modules.purpose: Gate assets on topology, transforms, naming, pivots, UVs, maps, materials, rigs, animation, LOD, collision, bounds, and platform budgets.
modules.whyNow: The factory needs one honest inspector that prevents weak previews or mislabeled files from becoming library assets.
modules.firstBuild: Validate the four Forge target families and explain every failure in human and machine form.
acceptance: Writer and validator implementations are independent
Impossible claims fail closed
Results bind to exact artifact digests
Visual quality remains a separate human gate

modules.name: Rigging & Retargeting Studio
modules.purpose: Author skeletons, skin weights, constraints, IK targets, sockets, humanoid mappings, retarget profiles, and deformation tests.
modules.whyNow: Four borrowed animated people are not a character-production system.
modules.firstBuild: Retarget the current 22-clip pedestrian set onto two visibly different body proportions.
acceptance: Joint mapping and rest-pose changes are explicit
Foot sliding and joint error are measured
Skin weights remain normalized
Human review covers extreme poses

modules.name: Modular Environment & Prop Kit Builder
modules.purpose: Author grid-snapped walls, floors, roofs, facades, interiors, doors, props, sockets, pivots, variants, damage states, and assembly rules as reusable families.
modules.whyNow: A few composed scenes do not yet provide enough coherent pieces to build many games quickly.
modules.firstBuild: Produce one street kit that can assemble ten distinct blocks without gaps or one-off fixes.
acceptance: Snap and connector contracts are deterministic
Every piece has pivot and bounds tests
Variant reuse is measured
Ten generated layouts pass gap and visual-coherence review

modules.name: Frame & Render Performance Profiler
modules.purpose: Measure CPU frame stages, GPU passes, shader compilation, draw calls, triangles, overdraw, texture traffic, stalls, percentiles, and frame spikes.
modules.whyNow: PS3-looking assets are useless if the runtime cannot explain why a scene stutters.
modules.firstBuild: Profile native and post-processed Forge scenes inside the 3D runtime on the current machine.
acceptance: Warm-up and measurement windows are separate
P50, P95, and worst-frame evidence is retained
Profiler overhead is declared
A frame screenshot links to its exact timing receipt

modules.name: Texture, Trim-sheet & Decal Studio
modules.purpose: Author tileable textures, trim sheets, atlases, masks, decals, signage, channel packs, mip-safe borders, and reusable material assignments.
modules.whyNow: Reusable surface language produces more visual quality per authored byte than thousands of unrelated textures.
modules.firstBuild: Create one urban trim sheet and decal family used by at least twenty modular environment pieces.
acceptance: Seams and mip bleed are checked
Channel semantics are declared
Atlas utilization is measured
In-engine close and distance views pass review

modules.name: Character & Creature Studio
modules.purpose: Build coherent body, face, clothing, hair, accessory, material, skeleton, LOD, collision, and variation families from editable recipes.
modules.whyNow: Games need recognisable casts, not four repeated stock pedestrians.
modules.firstBuild: Produce a ten-person civilian family with bounded shared parts and no automatic library promotion.
acceptance: Every variant remains attributable to source parts
Body and clothing intersections are tested
Rig and LOD contracts pass
Human review rejects uncanny or incoherent variants

modules.name: Character Animation, Mocap & Facial Studio
modules.purpose: Edit clips, clean captured motion, create blend spaces, root motion, events, facial poses, lip sync, additive layers, and compression profiles.
modules.whyNow: Retargeting only moves existing clips; games need editable performances and runtime-ready state data.
modules.firstBuild: Create idle, walk, run, turn, interact, talk, hit, fall, and recover sets for one rig.
acceptance: Foot and root drift are measured
Events survive export
Facial/audio timing is inspectable
Two live frame sequences prove transitions without pops

modules.name: Vehicle Assembly & Damage Studio
modules.purpose: Build vehicle bodies, interiors, wheels, suspension sockets, lights, materials, collision, occupants, LODs, detachable parts, and staged damage states.
modules.whyNow: The current source pool has vehicles but not a reusable, driveable, damage-aware production contract.
modules.firstBuild: Produce one hatchback family with intact, dented, broken-light, detached-door, and wreck states.
acceptance: Wheel and seat sockets match runtime coordinates
Collision and mass metadata validate
Damage transitions preserve lineage
Driving and impact tests are visually inspected

modules.name: Deterministic Build, Cook & Patch Pipeline
modules.purpose: Transform reviewed source assets and code into platform profiles, compiled shaders, cooked data, chunk manifests, signed packages, and reproducible patches.
modules.whyNow: A game factory needs one repeatable route from editable source to runnable package.
modules.firstBuild: Cook the first 3D runtime demo twice and prove byte-identical outputs from identical inputs.
acceptance: Input and toolchain digests are complete
Clean rebuilds are reproducible
Cancelled cooks leave no promoted partial output
Patch application verifies and rolls back

modules.name: World Partition & Streaming Compiler
modules.purpose: Compile large worlds into spatial cells, dependency bundles, visibility groups, streaming priorities, origin shifts, and memory-bounded load plans.
modules.whyNow: District Party's huge tiled map proves the view-range idea; a general 3D world needs the same authority at asset and runtime scale.
modules.firstBuild: Partition one city district and stream camera-visible cells plus a bounded margin.
acceptance: Cell membership is deterministic
Missing dependency edges fail compilation
Load/unload memory stays within the declared budget
Fast movement and reconnect tests show no persistent holes

modules.name: Physics, Destruction & Ragdoll Runtime
modules.purpose: Provide deterministic-enough rigid bodies, character controllers, joints, triggers, vehicles, ragdolls, damage events, and bounded destruction recipes.
modules.whyNow: Collision metadata alone does not create convincing interaction or damage gameplay.
modules.firstBuild: Walk, drive, collide, knock down a pedestrian, and break one reviewed prop without mutating source assets.
acceptance: Fixed-step replay stays within declared tolerance
Authority ownership is explicit
Extreme values fail safely
Visual motion and recovery are reviewed live

modules.name: Terrain, Foliage & Biome Studio
modules.purpose: Author terrain tiles, splat layers, roads, water masks, foliage rules, seasons, erosion recipes, collision, LOD, and biome transitions.
modules.whyNow: Foundation Planet needs authored land and ecological appearance that games can reuse without owning world state.
modules.firstBuild: Create a streamed temperate-to-urban transition with roads, foliage, water, and collision.
acceptance: Tile seams and normal continuity pass
Scatter is seeded and bounded
Runtime memory and draw budgets are measured
Seasonal views pass human coherence review

modules.name: Procedural City & Interior Studio
modules.purpose: Generate streets, lots, facades, interiors, doors, stairs, rooms, props, zoning, traversal links, and repairable layout recipes from modular kits.
modules.whyNow: Large game worlds need structured reuse, not hand-placing every building or retaining thousands of random variants.
modules.firstBuild: Generate one Tilburg-inspired district with ten enterable buildings from approved kits.
acceptance: Road and doorway connectivity validate
Only selected layouts are retained
Seed and kit versions reproduce the result
Human review covers navigability and visual repetition

modules.name: Navigation, Crowd & Behavior Studio
modules.purpose: Build navmeshes, links, avoidance, paths, behavior trees, perception, schedules, crowd LOD, traffic rules, and debuggable agent intent.
modules.whyNow: A populated GTA- or Diablo-like world needs agents that move and behave without consuming AI-model inference every frame.
modules.firstBuild: Run pedestrians and vehicles through one streamed district using deterministic local rules.
acceptance: Reachability and stuck-agent rates are measured
Agent decisions are inspectable
Crowd cost respects a declared budget
Door, crossing, traffic, and reconnect journeys pass live tests

modules.name: Gameplay Ability & Rules Graph
modules.purpose: Author events, conditions, actions, attributes, cooldowns, effects, interactions, objectives, scoring, and reusable rule sets without arbitrary code execution.
modules.whyNow: World state and physics need a safe designer-facing layer that turns a scene into a game.
modules.firstBuild: Create one collect, combat, interaction, and timed-objective loop from bounded graph nodes.
acceptance: Graphs validate types and cycles
Execution is deterministic under replay
Rules cannot claim world ownership
A non-programmer can inspect why an action fired

modules.name: VFX, Particle & Shader Graph Studio
modules.purpose: Author particles, trails, decals, flipbooks, dissolve, water, foliage, damage, weather, and bounded material shader graphs with platform profiles.
modules.whyNow: PS3-era presentation depends on effects and material behaviour, not just more polygons.
modules.firstBuild: Create rain, dust, impact, fire, smoke, water, and damage effects for the district demo.
acceptance: Shader graphs compile deterministically
Instruction, texture, and particle budgets are visible
Fallback profiles are explicit
Motion is visually checked across multiple frames

modules.name: Lighting, Probe & Lightmap Baker
modules.purpose: Author local lights, shadow profiles, reflection probes, irradiance volumes, lightmaps, time-of-day sets, and bake-validation recipes.
modules.whyNow: The current post stack improves presentation, but coherent PS3 scenes need reusable indirect-light and reflection data.
modules.firstBuild: Bake day and night lighting for the storefront and one streamed street cell.
acceptance: No invalid UV or probe coverage is hidden
Bake inputs reproduce exact outputs
Dynamic and baked lighting do not double-count
Reference views pass exposure and continuity review

modules.name: Reference-to-3D Reconstruction Lab
modules.purpose: Turn consented photos, drawings, dimensions, or multi-view references into editable geometry, calibrated cameras, materials, uncertainty masks, and source-linked recipes.
modules.whyNow: It gives humans and machines a faster path from real places or concept art to coherent source assets while keeping uncertainty visible.
modules.firstBuild: Reconstruct one simple facade and one prop from bounded multi-view references.
acceptance: Source rights and consent are recorded
Scale and camera calibration error are measured
Uncertain geometry is labeled
A human compares reconstruction against held-out views

modules.name: VRAM, Memory & Streaming Budget Analyzer
modules.purpose: Attribute CPU memory, GPU resources, textures, meshes, animation, caches, streamed cells, peaks, leaks, and eviction events to exact assets and systems.
modules.whyNow: Big worlds fail from residency and streaming mistakes long before average triangle counts explain the problem.
modules.firstBuild: Measure a camera journey across streamed district cells and identify the top ten residency costs.
acceptance: Peak and steady-state memory are separate
Resources trace back to asset digests
Eviction and reload events are recorded
Budget failures point to repairable owners

modules.name: Game UI, HUD & Menu Runtime
modules.purpose: Carry Studio-authored interfaces into games as resolution-safe HUDs, menus, maps, inventory, dialogue, settings, subtitles, focus, touch, and controller navigation.
modules.whyNow: UI assets already exist, but a real game needs one runtime contract instead of bespoke overlays per title.
modules.firstBuild: Create title, pause, settings, HUD, minimap, inventory, and result screens for the district demo.
acceptance: Keyboard, controller, and touch focus work
Resize and safe-area tests pass
Opening and closing overlays restores camera/input state
Accessibility labels and contrast are checked

modules.name: Quest, Dialogue & Narrative Runtime
modules.purpose: Author branching dialogue, quests, objectives, conditions, relationships, cutscene cues, localization keys, state migrations, and replayable narrative tests.
modules.whyNow: Most complete games need authored progression that survives save, localization, and changing world state.
modules.firstBuild: Build one multi-step district quest with two outcomes and a recoverable interruption.
acceptance: Unreachable and dead-end branches are detected
Narrative state serializes and migrates
Every line has stable localization identity
Complete and interrupted journeys pass live tests

modules.name: Save, Migration & Replay Service
modules.purpose: Own versioned game saves, checkpoints, schema migrations, deterministic input replays, corruption detection, preview restore, and compatibility receipts.
modules.whyNow: A persistent world is not the same thing as a player-safe game save and reproducible bug replay.
modules.firstBuild: Save, upgrade, replay, corrupt, detect, preview, and restore one district play session.
acceptance: Old fixtures migrate without silent loss
Corruption fails closed
Replay divergence is reported at the first mismatched tick
Restore never rewinds canonical world lineage

modules.name: Network Replication & Prediction Lab
modules.purpose: Define authoritative replication, interest management, snapshots, deltas, prediction, reconciliation, interpolation, packet loss simulation, anti-cheat boundaries, and reconnect.
modules.whyNow: Controller transport moves inputs, but multiplayer games still need shared game-state behavior under real latency and loss.
modules.firstBuild: Synchronize two moving players, one vehicle, and one destructible prop over simulated LAN faults.
acceptance: Server authority is explicit
Bandwidth and correction rates are measured
Loss and reorder tests recover
Two-display live evidence shows no hidden ownership confusion

modules.name: Dedicated Session Orchestrator
modules.purpose: Start, supervise, discover, join, migrate, stop, and receipt bounded local game sessions with ports, seats, maps, mods, rules, health, and recovery.
modules.whyNow: Each game should not reinvent service startup, port ownership, lobbies, and cleanup.
modules.firstBuild: Launch and cleanly stop a two-seat 3D district session from Game Hub.
acceptance: Port conflicts are refused or resolved visibly
Crash and reconnect paths are tested
No orphan process remains
Session receipts contain exact build and ruleset digests

modules.name: Input, Accessibility & Haptics Studio
modules.purpose: Author action maps, remapping, dead zones, chords, hold/toggle behavior, assists, difficulty access, subtitles, color filters, vibration, adaptive profiles, and device fallbacks.
modules.whyNow: Controls exist, but normal games need editable access and feedback profiles rather than hardcoded inputs.
modules.firstBuild: Ship complete keyboard, controller, phone, reduced-motion, high-contrast, subtitle, and no-haptics profiles for the demo.
acceptance: Every required action remains reachable
Profiles survive reconnect and resize
Haptics obey comfort and disable controls
Human accessibility review remains separately recorded

modules.name: Visual Art Director & Perceptual QA Lab
modules.purpose: Compare live assets and scenes against explicit style references for readability, coherence, repetition, silhouette, material response, lighting, era target, and visible defects.
modules.whyNow: Technical tests cannot explain why an asset still looks like Paint, feels inconsistent, or misses the intended console era.
modules.firstBuild: Evaluate the same Forge family across PS2 Native and PS3 Preview without granting approval authority.
acceptance: Every judgment cites visible evidence and criteria
Model votes remain advisory and attributed
Disagreement routes to repair
Mike's human vote remains independently visible

modules.name: Automated Playtester & Scenario Agent
modules.purpose: Run bounded player journeys, fuzz inputs, explore routes, record failures, preserve short visual evidence, reproduce seeds, and submit repair-ready bug receipts.
modules.whyNow: More games and larger worlds will outgrow purely manual traversal while still requiring live visual proof.
modules.firstBuild: Run entry-to-outcome journeys on one 3D demo and one District Party mode.
acceptance: Scenarios are bounded and reproducible
False completion is forbidden
Visual buffers are cleaned after selected proof frames
Human controls can stop or take over immediately

modules.name: Audio Listening & Quality Lab
modules.purpose: Measure and audition loudness, clipping, noise, dynamics, loops, spatial behavior, masking, dialogue clarity, subtitle sync, and mix translation.
modules.whyNow: Audio Studio can create sounds, but waveform existence does not prove that a game sounds good or remains intelligible.
modules.firstBuild: Evaluate a small game mix across effects, music, dialogue, mono, stereo, quiet, and loud conditions.
acceptance: Objective meters and listening judgments stay separate
Audible playback evidence is required
Clipping and loop seams are machine-detected
Human listening approval remains explicit

modules.name: Game Balance & Telemetry Advisor
modules.purpose: Analyze privacy-safe local playtest events, progression, difficulty, economy, win rates, churn points, exploits, and strategy diversity without composite player scoring.
modules.whyNow: A playable game still needs evidence that its rules are understandable, varied, and fair enough to keep playing.
modules.firstBuild: Compare at least twenty seeded bot/human demo runs while keeping identities pseudonymous and dimensions separate.
acceptance: Event schema excludes secrets and unnecessary identity
Recommendations link to exact runs
Uncertainty and sample size are visible
Design changes require review and new-digest evidence

modules.name: AI Tool & Skill Regression Harness
modules.purpose: Test hands, skills, tools, prompts, models, permissions, refusals, malformed inputs, long runs, and compatibility through versioned fixtures and exact receipts.
modules.whyNow: The AI Team has many tools, but adding more without stable behavioral regression tests creates silent capability drift.
modules.firstBuild: Create a core suite for capability detection, file edits, visual verification, refusal boundaries, and handoff contracts.
acceptance: Fixtures separate expected ability from model wording
Permissions are tested negatively
Provider/model versions are recorded
Regressions cannot be hidden by relaxed assertions

modules.name: Consent-bound Agent Memory & Dataset Curator
modules.purpose: Curate training, retrieval, evaluation, style, and project corpora with consent, provenance, redaction, deduplication, expiry, withdrawal, splits, and contamination checks.
modules.whyNow: Learning and memory become dangerous or useless when raw sessions, private material, duplicates, and unverifiable sources accumulate.
modules.firstBuild: Create one opt-in visual-style corpus and one separate regression set from explicitly approved Workshop artifacts.
acceptance: Consent and source rights bind to every item
Withdrawal removes future use without falsifying history
Train/evaluation contamination is checked
Raw private sessions are not silently retained

modules.name: Native Dependency Foundry
modules.purpose: Inventory external dependencies, rank replacement value, specify clean-room contracts, build AXM-native substitutes, compare behavior, and isolate optional compatibility adapters.
modules.whyNow: The explicit Workshop policy prefers ten thousand owned steps over one hidden or mandatory dependency.
modules.firstBuild: Map every runtime dependency used by game and asset production, then replace the smallest high-value one end to end.
acceptance: Inventory distinguishes required, vendored, optional, and development-only
Replacement contracts include failure and compatibility behavior
Parity tests use independent fixtures
Licenses and clean-room provenance are reviewed

modules.name: Codec & Container Foundry
modules.purpose: Implement and verify the bounded codecs, archive containers, image/audio/video chunks, compression primitives, and parsers AXM needs most, with fuzz-resistant readers.
modules.whyNow: Native WAV and ZIP are proven; visual game production still depends on more formats and must not fake containers by relabeling bytes.
modules.firstBuild: Harden existing ZIP/WAV, then add only the next format required by a blocked real request.
acceptance: Independent parsers verify every emitted container
Malformed and oversized inputs fail closed
Compression and decode budgets are measured
Optional external codecs never become silent requirements

modules.name: Schema, Contract & Migration Registry
modules.purpose: Catalog schemas and versions, resolve compatibility, validate references, generate fixtures, apply explicit migrations, preserve losses, and stop incompatible handoffs.
modules.whyNow: Hundreds of modular contracts will otherwise drift faster than humans or machines can safely compose them.
modules.firstBuild: Register module, asset, world, review, direction, and release schemas with forward and rollback fixtures.
acceptance: Every migration declares source, target, losses, and reversibility
Unknown versions fail visibly
Old fixtures remain readable
Migration receipts bind before/after digests

modules.name: Deterministic Job Queue & Artifact Cache
modules.purpose: Schedule bounded local CPU/GPU jobs, leases, priorities, cancellation, resumable chunks, content-addressed caching, invalidation, quotas, and receipts.
modules.whyNow: Baking, LODs, builds, tests, captures, and AI reviews need shared resource control instead of each module inventing a queue.
modules.firstBuild: Queue texture bakes, LOD builds, tests, and packaging with bounded concurrency and exact cache keys.
acceptance: Identical inputs reuse verified outputs
Changed inputs invalidate only affected work
Cancellation leaves recoverable state
Resource and wait-time receipts remain separate

modules.name: Crash, Replay & Symbolication Center
modules.purpose: Capture bounded crash metadata, source maps and symbols, exact builds, replay inputs, world revisions, last frames, deduplication, privacy redaction, and repair routing.
modules.whyNow: Large games and automated runs will produce failures that cannot be repaired from a generic error message.
modules.firstBuild: Reproduce and symbolicate one forced runtime crash and one deterministic desync from exact evidence.
acceptance: Secrets and unrelated content are excluded
Crash identity binds to exact build
Replay reaches the same first failure
Evidence retention stays bounded

modules.name: Source Control & Merge Workbench
modules.purpose: Show changes, ownership lanes, branches, conflicts, semantic manifest diffs, binary provenance, commits, rollback points, and reviewed GitHub handoff without destructive defaults.
modules.whyNow: Many AI chats and humans already edit one live workspace; the Hub needs a beginner-safe merge surface before major GitHub updates.
modules.firstBuild: Review and commit one multi-module update while preserving unrelated concurrent changes.
acceptance: Dirty state is never treated as disposable
Conflicts show both owners and exact semantics
Commits include deliberate scope and tests
Push and PR actions remain explicit

modules.name: Security, Fuzz & Supply-chain Lab
modules.purpose: Fuzz parsers and contracts, inspect attack surfaces, permissions, secrets, path traversal, archive bombs, unsafe deserialization, dependency provenance, sandbox escapes, and denial-of-service budgets.
modules.whyNow: A modular open platform becomes easier to harm through malformed inputs and plugins unless negative testing grows with capability.
modules.firstBuild: Fuzz module bundles, asset containers, world patches, save files, and review payloads in isolated temporary roots.
acceptance: Seed corpora and crashes are reproducible
Tests cannot reach unrelated workspace paths
Resource exhaustion has explicit limits
Findings route to repair without publishing exploit payloads by default

modules.name: License, Rights & Attribution Auditor
modules.purpose: Trace code, assets, fonts, audio, data, models, derivatives, consent, licenses, attribution, redistribution terms, conflicts, and unknown rights before promotion.
modules.whyNow: Free/open-source goals fail if one attractive intake or generated derivative has unclear publication rights.
modules.firstBuild: Audit the PS2 Forge source packs, generated code, staged PS3 intake, and one complete game package.
acceptance: Every shipped artifact has a traceable rights state
Unknown never becomes allowed
Required notices are generated exactly
Human/legal approval remains explicit

modules.name: Reproducible Build, SBOM & Provenance Generator
modules.purpose: Produce exact source, toolchain, license, schema, dependency, build-step, artifact, signature, and verification manifests for public packages.
modules.whyNow: A signed ZIP is not enough when users and future stewards need to rebuild and understand what it contains.
modules.firstBuild: Rebuild one game release twice and emit a complete machine-readable provenance bill.
acceptance: Independent rebuilds match or explain every difference
All included files appear in the inventory
Toolchain versions and licenses are bound
Private paths, logs, secrets, and user state are absent

modules.name: Release Size, Compression & Delta Patch Optimizer
modules.purpose: Analyze package size, duplicates, compression, chunk layout, optional content, patches, rollback payloads, cache reuse, and install-time budgets without quality-damaging defaults.
modules.whyNow: Large assets and frequent updates become noise when every release retransmits the whole Workshop or silently crushes quality.
modules.firstBuild: Create a verified delta between two district-demo releases and restore both versions.
acceptance: Installed output matches the target digest
Patch and rollback are interruption-tested
Quality-changing compression needs approval
Size savings are reported by content family

modules.name: Marketplace Compatibility & Sandbox Certifier
modules.purpose: Run module, plugin, game, asset, permission, lifecycle, performance, accessibility, malware, install, update, removal, and rollback profiles before catalog admission.
modules.whyNow: A marketplace needs stronger evidence than a manifest and attractive gallery card.
modules.firstBuild: Certify one module, one asset pack, and one game package in clean temporary sandboxes.
acceptance: Certification profiles are versioned
Negative and uninstall tests run
Authority and network use match declarations
Certification can expire or be revoked without deleting provenance

modules.name: Documentation, Tutorial & Capture Studio
modules.purpose: Create version-bound manuals, onboarding, tutorials, screenshots, comparison views, controller diagrams, accessibility notes, release videos, and machine-readable help from verified workflows.
modules.whyNow: Power nobody can understand produces noise; beginners need visible outcomes and exact actions rather than internal evidence counters.
modules.firstBuild: Produce a five-minute PS2 Asset Forge-to-playable-demo tutorial with exact version and proof links.
acceptance: Every instruction is replayed on the shipped build
Screens and labels match the current UI
Media is rights-cleared
Beginner and machine handoffs are both tested

modules.name: Localization, Subtitle & Store-metadata Release Pipeline
modules.purpose: Manage stable message IDs, translations, fonts, layout expansion, plural rules, subtitles, dubbing cues, store text, screenshots, regional packages, review, and fallback behavior.
modules.whyNow: Normal public software cannot treat language, readable subtitles, and regional metadata as a last-minute text replacement.
modules.firstBuild: Ship English and Dutch demo packages with tested subtitles, UI expansion, fallback, and store metadata.
acceptance: Missing and stale translations are detected
Font shaping and overflow are visually checked
Subtitle timing and speaker identity are verified
Fallback never exposes raw keys or private source text
